q-36390.name: Question 1
q-36390.problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z)=8x-{y}^{2}-z$, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes  through the point where $(x,y,z)=(2,4,1).$
q-36390.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(2,4,1):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(8x-{y}^{2}-z)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(8x-{y}^{2}-z)\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(8x-{y}^{2}-z)\text{ }k \\  & =8\text{ }i-2y\text{ }j-k \\ ∇\,f(2,4,1) & =8\text{ }i-2(4)\text{ }j-k \\  & =8\,i-8\,j-k \\  & =⟨8,-8,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(2,4,1)\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y-4,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨8,-8,-1⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y-4,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ 8(x-2)-8(y-4)-(z-1) & =0 \\ 8x-8y-z+17 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Given the function f(x,y,z)=8x−y2−z, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes through the point where (x,y,z)=(2,4,1).

a
2x−8y−3z+4=0
b
x−y−z+17=0
c
x−8y−z+7=0
d
8x−y−z+27=0
e
8x−8y−z+17=0
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface f(x,y,z)=k at the point (x0,y0,z0) can be expressed as

∇f(x0,y0,z0)⋅⟨x−x0,y−y0,z−z0⟩=0.

First, we find the gradient of f(x,y,z) and evaluate it at (x0,y0,z0)=(2,4,1):

∇f(x,y,z)=fx(x,y,z)i+fy(x,y,z)j+fz(x,y,z)k=∂∂x(8x−y2−z) i+∂∂y(8x−y2−z) j+∂∂z(8x−y2−z) k=8 i−2y j−k∇f(2,4,1)=8 i−2(4) j−k=8i−8j−k=⟨8,−8,−1⟩

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

∇f(x0,y0,z0)⋅⟨x−x0,y−y0,z−z0⟩=0∇f(2,4,1)⋅⟨x−2,y−4,z−1⟩=0⟨8,−8,−1⟩⋅⟨x−2,y−4,z−1⟩=08(x−2)−8(y−4)−(z−1)=08x−8y−z+17=0

q-102702.name: Question 2
q-102702.problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z)={e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+{z}^{2}$, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes  through the point where $(x,y,z)=(\frac{\pi }{4},4,1).$
q-102702.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(\frac{\pi }{4},4,1):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+{z}^{2})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+{z}^{2})\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+{z}^{2})\text{ }k \\  & =-2{e}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x\text{ }i+{e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x\text{ }j+2zk \\ ∇\,f(\frac{\pi }{4},4,1) & =-2{e}^{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})\text{ }i+{e}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})\text{ }j+2(1)k \\  & =-2{e}^{4}\,i+0\,j+2k \\  & =⟨-2{e}^{4},0,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(\frac{\pi }{4},4,1)\cdot ⟨x-\frac{\pi }{4},\,y-4,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-2{e}^{4},0,2⟩\cdot ⟨x-\frac{\pi }{4},\,y-4,\,z-1⟩ & =0\end{aligned}
$$

q-102707.name: Question 3
q-102707.problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}z+{z}^{2}y+{y}^{2}x$, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes  through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,1,-1).$
q-102707.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(1,1,-1):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}z+{z}^{2}y+{y}^{2}x)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}z+{z}^{2}y+{y}^{2}x)\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}z+{z}^{2}y+{y}^{2}x)\text{ }k \\  & =(2xz+{y}^{2})\text{ }i+({z}^{2}+2yx)\text{ }j+({x}^{2}+2zy)k \\ ∇\,f(1,1,-1) & =(2(1)(-1)+{1}^{2})\text{ }i+((-1)^{2}+2(1)(1))\text{ }j+({1}^{2}+2(-1)(1))k \\  & =-\,i+3\,j-k \\  & =⟨-1,3,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(1,1,-1)\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-1,\,z+1⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-1,3,-1⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-1,\,z+1⟩ & =0 \\ -(x-1)+3(y-1)-(z+1) & =0 \\ -x+3y-z-3 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

q-102703.problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z)=x{z}^{2}+z{y}^{3}$, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes  through the point where $(x,y,z)=(-2,1,2).$
q-102703.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(-2,1,2):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{z}^{2}+z{y}^{3})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{z}^{2}+z{y}^{3})\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(x{z}^{2}+z{y}^{3})\text{ }k \\  & ={z}^{2}\text{ }i+3z{y}^{2}\text{ }j+(2xz+{y}^{3})k \\ ∇\,f(-2,1,2) & ={2}^{2}\text{ }i+3(2)(1)^{2}\text{ }j+(2(-2)(2)+{1}^{3})k \\  & =4\,i+6\,j-7k \\  & =⟨4,6,-7⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(-2,1,2)\cdot ⟨x+2,\,y-1,\,z-2⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨4,6,-7⟩\cdot ⟨x+2,\,y-1,\,z-2⟩ & =0 \\ 4(x+2)+6(y-1)-7(z-2) & =0 \\ 4x+6y-7z+16 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

q-36334.problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z)=x{e}^{y}-z$, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,1,e).$
q-36334.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(1,1,e):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{e}^{y}-z)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{e}^{y}-z)\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(x{e}^{y}-z)\text{ }k \\  & ={e}^{y}\text{ }i+x{e}^{y}\text{ }j-k \\ ∇\,f(1,1,e) & ={e}^{1}\text{ }i+(1){e}^{1}\text{ }j-k \\  & =e\,i+e\,j-k \\  & =⟨e,e,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(1,1,e)\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-1,\,z-e⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨e,e,-1⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-1,\,z-e⟩ & =0\end{aligned}
$$

q-80778.problem: Consider the surface ${2}^{3{z}^{2}+2xy}=2.$ Given that $n=⟨a,b,c⟩$ is a non-zero normal vector to the surface at the point $(1,-1,1),$ what is the value of $\frac{c}{b}?$
q-80778.worked_solution:
Let's define  $f(x,y,z)={2}^{3{z}^{2}+2xy}.$ Then, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=2.$  

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(1,-1,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({2}^{3{z}^{2}+2xy})i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({2}^{3{z}^{2}+2xy})j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({2}^{3{z}^{2}+2xy})k \\  & =({2}^{3{z}^{2}+2xy}\cdot 2y\operatorname{ln}⁡2)i+({2}^{3{z}^{2}+2xy}\cdot 2x\operatorname{ln}⁡2)j+({2}^{3{z}^{2}+2xy}\cdot 6z\operatorname{ln}⁡2)k \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡2(y\,\text{ }{2}^{3{z}^{2}+2xy}\text{ }i+x\,\text{ }{2}^{3{z}^{2}+2xy}\text{ }j+3z\,\text{ }{2}^{3{z}^{2}+2xy}\text{ }k) \\ ∇f(1,-1,1) & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡2((-1)\cdot \text{ }{2}^{3(1)^{2}+2\cdot 1\cdot (-1)}\text{ }i+1\cdot \,\text{ }{2}^{3(1)^{2}+2\cdot 1\cdot (-1)}\text{ }j+3(1)\cdot {2}^{3(1)^{2}+2\cdot 1\cdot (-1)}\text{ }k) \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡2(-{2}^{1}\text{ }i+{2}^{1}\text{ }j+3\cdot {2}^{1}\text{ }k) \\  & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡2(-i+j+3\text{ }k) \\  & =⟨-4\operatorname{ln}⁡2,\,4\operatorname{ln}⁡2,\,12\operatorname{ln}⁡2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩=⟨-4\operatorname{ln}⁡2,\,4\operatorname{ln}⁡2,\,12\operatorname{ln}⁡2⟩.$

Finally, $\frac{c}{b}=\frac{12\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡2}=3.$

q-36764.problem: Consider the surface ${z}^{2}{x}^{2}=xy.$ Find the equation of the tangent plane to that surface at the point $(1,4,2).$
q-36764.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{2}{x}^{2} & =xy \\ {z}^{2}{x}^{2}-xy & =0\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y,z)={z}^{2}{x}^{2}-xy$, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=0.$ 

Recall that the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(1,4,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({z}^{2}{x}^{2}-xy)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({z}^{2}{x}^{2}-xy)\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({z}^{2}{x}^{2}-xy)\text{ }k \\  & =(2x{z}^{2}-y)\text{ }i-x\text{ }j+2{x}^{2}z\text{ }k \\ ∇\,f(1,4,2) & =(2(1)(2)^{2}-4)\text{ }i-(1)\text{ }j+2(1)^{2}(2)\text{ }k \\  & =4\,i-j+4\,k \\  & =⟨4,-1,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(1,4,2)\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-4,\,z-2⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨4,-1,4⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-4,\,z-2⟩ & =0 \\ 4(x-1)-(y-4)+4(z-2) & =0 \\ 4x-y+4z-8 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

q-102713.problem: Consider the surface $z\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)-xyz=2+\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{2}.$ Given that $n=⟨a,b,c⟩$ is a non-zero normal vector to the surface at the point $(\frac{\pi }{2},-\frac{\pi }{2},2),$ what is the value of $\frac{a}{b}?$
q-102713.worked_solution:
Let's define  $f(x,y,z)=z\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)-xyz.$ Then, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=2+\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{2}.$  

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(\frac{\pi }{2},-\frac{\pi }{2},2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(z\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)-xyz)i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(z\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)-xyz)j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(z\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)-xyz)k \\  & =(-z\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)-yz)i+(-z\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)-xz)j+(\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)-xy)k \\ ∇f(\frac{\pi }{2},-\frac{\pi }{2},2) & =(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{\pi }{2})-2(-\frac{\pi }{2}))\text{ }i+(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{\pi }{2})-2(\frac{\pi }{2}))\text{ }j+(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{\pi }{2})-(\frac{\pi }{2})(-\frac{\pi }{2}))\text{ }k \\  & =\pi \text{ }i-\pi \text{ }j+(1+\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{4})\text{ }k \\  & =⟨\pi ,\,-\pi ,\,1+\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{4}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩=⟨\pi ,\,-\pi ,\,\frac{{\pi }^{2}+4}{4}⟩.$

Finally, $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{\pi }{-\pi }=-1.$

Consider the surface zcos⁡(x+y)−xyz=2+π22. Given that n=⟨a,b,c⟩ is a non-zero normal vector to the surface at the point (π2,−π2,2), what is the value of ab?

a
 −1
b
 4
c
 4π2
d
 4π
e
 π
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's define f(x,y,z)=zcos⁡(x+y)−xyz. Then, our surface can be viewed as the level surface f(x,y,z)=2+π22.

Now, we find the gradient of f(x,y,z) and evaluate it at (π2,−π2,2):

∇f(x,y,z)=fx(x,y,z)i+fy(x,y,z)j+fz(x,y,z)k=∂∂x(zcos⁡(x+y)−xyz)i+∂∂y(zcos⁡(x+y)−xyz)j+∂∂z(zcos⁡(x+y)−xyz)k=(−zsin⁡(x+y)−yz)i+(−zsin⁡(x+y)−xz)j+(cos⁡(x+y)−xy)k∇f(π2,−π2,2)=(−2sin⁡(π2−π2)−2(−π2)) i+(−2sin⁡(π2−π2)−2(π2)) j+(cos⁡(π2−π2)−(π2)(−π2)) k=π i−π j+(1+π24) k=⟨π,−π,1+π24⟩

Therefore, our normal vector is n=⟨a,b,c⟩=⟨π,−π,π2+44⟩.

Finally, ab=π−π=−1.

q-102712.problem: Consider the surface ${z}^{2}y+16=4\sqrt{x}+y.$ Find the equation of the tangent plane to that surface at the point $(4,-1,3).$
q-102712.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{2}y+16 & =4\sqrt{x}+y. \\ {z}^{2}y-4\sqrt{x}-y & =-16\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y,z)={z}^{2}y-4\sqrt{x}-y$, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=-16.$ 

Recall that the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(4,-1,3):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({z}^{2}y-4\sqrt{x}-y)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({z}^{2}y-4\sqrt{x}-y)\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({z}^{2}y-4\sqrt{x}-y)\text{ }k \\  & =-\frac{2}{\sqrt{x}}\text{ }i+({z}^{2}-1)\text{ }j+2zy\text{ }k \\ ∇\,f(4,-1,3) & =-\frac{2}{\sqrt{4}}\text{ }i+({3}^{2}-1)\text{ }j+2(3)(-1)\text{ }k \\  & =-\,i+8\text{ }j-6\,k \\  & =⟨-1,8,-6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(4,-1,3)\cdot ⟨x-4,\,y+1,\,z-3⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-1,8,-6⟩\cdot ⟨x-4,\,y+1,\,z-3⟩ & =0 \\ -(x-4)+8(y+1)-6(z-3) & =0 \\ -x+8y-6z+30 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

q-102714.problem: Consider the surface $x{y}^{2}+6=z{x}^{2}.$ Find the equation of the tangent plane to that surface at the point $(-2,-1,1).$
q-102714.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x{y}^{2}+6 & =z{x}^{2} \\ x{y}^{2}-z{x}^{2} & =-6\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y,z)=x{y}^{2}-z{x}^{2}$, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=-6.$ 

Recall that the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(-2,-1,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{y}^{2}-z{x}^{2})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{y}^{2}-z{x}^{2})\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(x{y}^{2}-z{x}^{2})\text{ }k \\  & =({y}^{2}-2xz)\text{ }i+2xy\text{ }j-{x}^{2}\text{ }k \\ ∇\,f(-2,-1,1) & =((-1)^{2}-2(-2)(1))\text{ }i+2(-2)(-1)\text{ }j-(-2)^{2}\text{ }k \\  & =5\,i+4j-4\,k \\  & =⟨5,4,-4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(-2,-1,1)\cdot ⟨x+2,\,y+1,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨5,4,-4⟩\cdot ⟨x+2,\,y+1,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ 5(x+2)+4(y+1)-4(z-1) & =0 \\ 5x+4y-4z+18 & =0\end{aligned}

Question 10

Consider the surface xy2+6=zx2. Find the equation of the tangent plane to that surface at the point (−2,−1,1).

a
 x+2y−4z+15=0
b
 3x+4y+z−10=0
c
 x−y−3z+11=0
d
 5x−3y+2z−11=0
e
 5x+4y−4z+18=0
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we bring all variables to one side:

xy2+6=zx2xy2−zx2=−6

If we set f(x,y,z)=xy2−zx2, our surface can be viewed as the level surface f(x,y,z)=−6.

Recall that the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface f(x,y,z)=k at the point (x0,y0,z0) can be expressed as

∇f(x0,y0,z0)⋅⟨x−x0,y−y0,z−z0⟩=0.

Now, we find the gradient of f(x,y,z) and evaluate it at (−2,−1,1):

∇f(x,y,z)=fx(x,y,z)i+fy(x,y,z)j+fz(x,y,z)k=∂∂x(xy2−zx2) i+∂∂y(xy2−zx2) j+∂∂z(xy2−zx2) k=(y2−2xz) i+2xy j−x2 k∇f(−2,−1,1)=((−1)2−2(−2)(1)) i+2(−2)(−1) j−(−2)2 k=5i+4j−4k=⟨5,4,−4⟩

Finally, we can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

∇f(x0,y0,z0)⋅⟨x−x0,y−y0,z−z0⟩=0∇f(−2,−1,1)⋅⟨x+2,y+1,z−1⟩=0⟨5,4,−4⟩⋅⟨x+2,y+1,z−1⟩=05(x+2)+4(y+1)−4(z−1)=05x+4y−4z+18=0
